To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

adenoviruses with E1A deletions do not exhibit selectivity for HPV E6E and E7 expressing cells, whereas an adenovirus with deletions of both the CR1 and the CR2 domains of the E1A protein exhibits preferential replication in HPV E6 and E71 expressing cultures.

the adenovirus mutants described in this paper, and others that have been described in the past, are all deficient in their ability to selectively kill cells expressing HPV E6E 7 oncoproteints.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
adenoviruses deleted in E1A and/or E1B genes are unable to kill HPV 18 E6E 7 expressing cells in organotypic cultures of keratinocytes.
, whereas the adenovirus E1A protein is necessary for efficient adenovirus replication, it can also be a limiting factor for virus spread in the presence of HPV E6E and E7 onco-proteins.

adenovirus mutants that are deleted in the CR3 domain of E1a and that express a mutant E4orf6 protein that is not able to interact with p53 are the most promising candidates for the design of an oncolytic adenocin virus.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of organotypic cultures of primary human keratinocytes represents an excellent model to evaluate the selectivity of adenovirus replication and cell killing and that further modifications of the viral genome are required to achieve exclusive replication of the virus in tumor cells.
the organotypically derived keratinocyte culture system represents a distinct model system to evaluate adenoviruses for their potential to replicate and kill tumor cells selectively.
